CLKCTRLGeneric Clock Controlp. 100

offset 0x2 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W

  • Sets up the generic clock named in CLKCTRL.ID. Write it as one 16-bit access holding the whole setup and the ID. To read one clock's setup, first write its ID to CLKCTRL.ID with an 8-bit access, then read CLKCTRL.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15WRTLOCKR/W0Writing it locks the generic clock chosen by CLKCTRL.ID, the generator chosen by CLKCTRL.GEN and that generator's division factor against further writes, until a power reset. Generator 0 cannot be locked.
0Clock, generator and division factor unlocked.
1Clock, generator and division factor locked.
14CLKENR/W0Turns the generic clock on or off.
0Generic clock off.
1Generic clock on.
11:8GENR/W0x0Which generic clock generator feeds this clock: 0x0-0x5 pick GCLK0-GCLK5; 0x6-0xF reserved.
0x0GCLK0Generator 0 (GCLK0).
0x1GCLK1Generator 1 (GCLK1).
0x2GCLK2Generator 2 (GCLK2).
0x3GCLK3Generator 3 (GCLK3).
0x4GCLK4Generator 4 (GCLK4).
0x5GCLK5Generator 5 (GCLK5).
0x6-0xFReserved.
5:0IDR/W0x0Picks the generic clock that the CLKCTRL write sets up. A power reset clears CLKCTRL for every ID, RTC included; a user reset clears it for one ID only when that ID's WRTLOCK is 0 and the ID is not the RTC. After a power reset: RTC has GEN 0x00, CLKEN 0, WRTLOCK 0; WDT has GEN 0x02, CLKEN equal to the WDT Enable bit of the NVM User Row and WRTLOCK equal to its WDT Always-On bit; every other ID has GEN 0x00, CLKEN 0, WRTLOCK 0. After a user reset: RTC's GEN and CLKEN go to 0x00 when WRTLOCK=0 and CLKEN=0, otherwise stay; WDT's GEN goes to 0x02 and its CLKEN to the NVM User Row WDT Enable bit when WRTLOCK=0, otherwise both stay; every other ID's GEN and CLKEN go to 0x00 when WRTLOCK=0, otherwise stay; WRTLOCK never changes on a user reset.
0x0GCLK_DFLL48M_REFDFLL48M reference.
0x1GCLK_DPLLFDPLL96M reference input.
0x2GCLK_DPLL_32K32 kHz clock for the FDPLL96M internal lock timer.
0x3GCLK_WDTWDT.
0x4GCLK_RTCRTC.
0x5GCLK_EICEIC.
0x6Reserved.

GENCTRLGeneric Clock Generator Controlp. 103

offset 0x4 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

  • Sets up the generator named in GENCTRL.ID. Write it as one 32-bit access holding the whole setup and the ID. To read one generator's setup, first write its ID to GENCTRL.ID with an 8-bit access, then read GENCTRL.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
21RUNSTDBYR/W0Keeps the generator running in standby when it drives its GCLK_IO pin. With GENCTRL.OE at 0 it has no effect, and the generator runs only when a peripheral asks for its clock.
0Generator stops in standby; GCLK_IO then sits at the level GENCTRL.OOV sets.
1Generator keeps running in standby and keeps driving its GCLK_IO pin.
20DIVSELR/W0Chooses how the generator divides its source. For no division, DIVSEL must be 0 and the generator's GENDIV.DIV 0 or 1.
0Source divided by GENDIV.DIV.
1Source divided by 2^(GENDIV.DIV+1).
19OER/W0Sends the generator's clock out on GCLK_IO, when GCLK_IO is not chosen as the source in GENCTRL.SRC.
0Generator clock not sent out.
1Generator clock driven onto its GCLK_IO, unless that GCLK_IO is chosen as the source in GENCTRL.SRC.
18OOVR/W0Sets the level GCLK_IO holds when it is not chosen as the source in GENCTRL.SRC.
0GCLK_IO low while the generator is off or OE is 0.
1GCLK_IO high while the generator is off or OE is 0.
17IDCR/W0Evens out the generator's duty cycle when the division factor is odd.
0Duty cycle not 50/50 with odd division factors.
1Duty cycle 50/50.
16GENENR/W0Turns the generic clock generator on or off.
0Generator off.
1Generator on.
12:8SRCR/W0x0Clock source the generator runs from.
0x00XOSCXOSC output.
0x01GCLKINGenerator input pad.
0x02GCLKGEN1Output of generic clock generator 1.
0x03OSCULP32KOSCULP32K output.
0x04OSC32KOSC32K output.
0x05XOSC32KXOSC32K output.
0x06OSC8MOSC8M output.
0x07DFLL48MDFLL48M output.
0x08FDPLL96MFDPLL96M output.
0x09-0x1FReservedReserved.
3:0IDR/W0x0Which generic clock generator is being set up or read. A power reset resets GENCTRL for every ID, including the RTC's generator; a user reset resets it for any generator other than 0 that is not the source of a locked generic clock or of the RTC clock. Power-reset values: 0x00 0x00010600, 0x01 0x00000001, 0x02 0x00010302, 0x03 0x00000003, 0x04 0x00000004, 0x05 0x00000005; after a user reset generator 0 returns to 0x00010600 and generators 1-5 to these values unless used by the RTC or by a GCLK with WRTLOCK at 1, which keep theirs.
0x0GCLKGEN0Generator 0.
0x1GCLKGEN1Generator 1.
0x2GCLKGEN2Generator 2.
0x3GCLKGEN3Generator 3.
0x4GCLKGEN4Generator 4.
0x5GCLKGEN5Generator 5.
0x6-0xFReserved.

GENDIVGeneric Clock Generator Divisionp. 107

offset 0x8 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

  • Sets the division of the generator named in GENDIV.ID. Write it as one 32-bit access holding the factor and the ID. To read one generator's factor, first write its ID to GENDIV.ID with an 8-bit access, then read GENDIV.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
23:8DIVR/W0x0Division factor for the chosen generator. Width per generator: 0 has 8 bits (DIV[7:0]), 1 has 16 (DIV[15:0]), 2 has 5 (DIV[4:0]), 3-8 have 8 (DIV[7:0]); writes to higher bits are ignored.
3:0IDR/W0x0Which generic clock generator the division factor goes to. A power reset resets GENDIV for every ID, including the RTC's generator; a user reset resets it for any generator other than 0 that is not the source of a locked generic clock or of the RTC clock. Power-reset values: 0x00 0x00000000, and generator n (1-5) 0x0000000n; after a user reset generator 0 returns to 0x00000000 and generators 1-5 to 0x0000000n unless used by the RTC or by a GCLK with WRTLOCK at 1, which keep theirs.
0x0GCLKGEN0Generator 0.
0x1GCLKGEN1Generator 1.
0x2GCLKGEN2Generator 2.
0x3GCLKGEN3Generator 3.
0x4GCLKGEN4Generator 4.
0x5GCLKGEN5Generator 5.
0x6-0xFReserved.

CTRLAControl Ap. 365

offset 0x00 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15:8CMDEXR/W0x0Key for running the command in CMD: 0xA5 lets it run, written in the same access as CMD; any other key, or a write while an earlier command is unfinished, drops the write and sets PROGE. READY must be 1 when the command is issued. An APB command that coincides with an AHB access waits until the AHB access and the NVM block are idle. Bit 0 reads 1 until the command has been issued.
0x0-0xa4Reserved.
0xA5KEYKey that lets the command run.
0xa6-0xffReserved.
6:0CMDR/W0x0Command that runs when the CMDEX key is written.
0x0-0x1Reserved.
0x2ERErase Row: erases the row at the address in ADDR.
0x3Reserved.
0x4WPWrite Page: writes the page buffer into the page at the address in ADDR.
0x5EARErase Auxiliary Row: erases the auxiliary row at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear, and only for the user configuration row.
0x6WAPWrite Auxiliary Page: writes the page buffer into the auxiliary page at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear, and only for the user configuration row.
0x7-0x9Reserved.
0xASFSF: security flow command.
0xb-0xeReserved.
0xFWLWL: write the lock bits.
0x10-0x3fReserved.
0x40LRLock Region: locks the region holding the address in ADDR.
0x41URUnlock Region: unlocks the region holding the address in ADDR.
0x42SPRMSPRM: turn power reduction mode on.
0x43CPRMCPRM: turn power reduction mode off.
0x44PBCPBC: empty the page buffer.
0x45SSBSet Security Bit: a 0x00 is written into the first byte of the lockbit row, which turns the security bit on.
0x46INVALLINVALL: invalidate every cache line.
0x47-0x7fReserved.

CTRLBControl Bp. 367

offset 0x04 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
18CACHEDISR/W0Turns the NVM cache off when set.
0Cache on.
1Cache off.
17:16READMODER/W0x0Cache read mode. 0x0 NO_MISS_PENALTY: no wait state on a cache miss; the highest system performance. 0x1 LOW_POWER: lower cache power, but each miss adds a wait state that stalls the application and can lengthen run time, so it may not suit code that needs CPU performance. 0x2 DETERMINISTIC: a hit and a miss take equal time, set by the programmed flash wait states; for real-time code that needs deterministic timing. 0x3 is reserved.
0x0NO_MISS_PENALTYNo wait state is added on a cache miss; best system performance.
0x1LOW_POWERLower cache power, with one wait state added on every cache miss; the stalled CPU can make run time longer.
0x2DETERMINISTICCache hits and misses take equal time, set by the programmed flash wait states; for real-time code needing fixed timing.
0x3Reserved.
9:8SLEEPPRMR/W0x0How the NVM block saves power in sleep. 0x0 WAKEONACCESS: low-power on entering sleep, out of it on the first access. 0x1 WAKEUPINSTANT: low-power on entering sleep, out of it on leaving sleep. 0x3 DISABLED: no automatic power reduction. 0x2 is reserved.
0x0WAKEONACCESSNVM goes to low power on sleep and leaves it at the first access.
0x1WAKEUPINSTANTNVM goes to low power on sleep and leaves it on wake from sleep.
0x2Reserved.
0x3DISABLEDNo automatic power reduction.

0A write to the last word of the page buffer starts writing the page at the last written address.
1Writes start only from a command in CMD.
4:1RWSR/W0x0Number of wait states added to an NVM read, 0 to 15; resets to 0. Software sets it to suit the NVM access time and the system clock frequency.

7ERRORR/W0Set when an error is found. The errors are LENERR, SEXTTOUT, MEXTTOUT, LOWTOUT, ARBLOST or BUSERR, and each has its own flag in STATUS. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.
1SBR/W0Set when the master receives a byte in master read mode without lost arbitration or bus error; the master then holds SCL low, stretching the clock. SCL is let go and the flag cleared by a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with smart mode on (CTRLB.SMEN), or a valid command written to CTRLB.CMD. Writing 1 clears SB too; writing 0 does nothing. The transaction neither goes on nor ends until one of those actions.
0MBR/W0Set when the master sends a byte in master write mode, whether or not a bus error or lost arbitration happened; also set when arbitration is lost while sending a NACK in master read mode, and when a START is issued with the bus state unknown. While set without lost arbitration, the master holds SCL low, stretching the clock. SCL is let go and the flag cleared by a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with smart mode on (CTRLB.SMEN), or a valid command written to CTRLB.CMD. Writing 1 clears MB too, whether or not arbitration was lost; writing 0 does nothing. The transaction neither goes on nor ends until one of those actions.

STATUSStatusp. 564

offset 0x1A · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R, R, R/W, R/W · write-synchronized

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
10LENERRR/W0Set when, with automatic length used for a DMA transaction, the slave sends NACK before the master has written ADDR.LEN bytes. Cleared on its own when ADDR is written. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.
9SEXTTOUTR/W0Set when a slave SCL low extend time-out happens. Normal use does not need it cleared by writing 1. Cleared on its own when ADDR is written. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.
8MEXTTOUTR/W0Set when a master SCL low time-out happens. Normal use does not need it cleared by writing 1. Cleared on its own when ADDR is written. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.
7CLKHOLDR0Set while the master holds SCL low to stretch the clock. It is a read-only status, set together with INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB, and cleared once that interrupt flag is cleared and a following operation starts. Writes of 0 or 1 do nothing. Not write-synchronized.
6LOWTOUTR/W0Set when an SCL low time-out happens. Normal use does not need it cleared by writing 1. Cleared on its own when ADDR is written. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.
5:4BUSSTATER, R/W0x0Shows the I2C bus state; it is unknown after the master is enabled and whenever the master is disabled. 0x0 Unknown: the master waits to see a STOP or to be forced to idle by software. 0x1 Idle: waiting for a transaction to start. 0x2 Owner: this master owns the bus. 0x3 Busy: another master owns the bus. From unknown, writing 0x1 forces the state to idle; no other state can be forced. Writing idle sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY.
0x0UnknownUnknown: the master waits until it sees a stop condition or software forces the bus to idle.
0x1IdleIdle: no transaction has started on the bus.
0x2OwnerOwner: this master holds the bus.
0x3BusyBusy: another master holds the bus.
2RXNACKR0Tells whether the slave acknowledged the last address or data packet sent. Writes of 0 or 1 do nothing. Not write-synchronized.
0Slave gave ACK.
1Slave gave NACK.
1ARBLOSTR/W0Set when arbitration is lost while sending a high data bit or a NACK, or during a START or repeated START; INTFLAG.MB is set with it. A write to ADDR.ADDR clears it, as does writing 1; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.
0BUSERRR/W0Set when an illegal condition appears on the bus, whoever owns it: a START, repeated START or STOP that breaks the protocol (a START straight followed by a STOP is one), or a time-out during a frame. If the master owns the bus when it happens, STATUS.ARBLOST and INTFLAG.MB are set too. A write to ADDR.ADDR clears it, as does writing 1; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

ADDRAddressp. 569

offset 0x24 · 32 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W · write-synchronized

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
23:16LENR/W0x0Number of bytes in a DMA transaction, 0 to 255. Used only when ADDR.LENEN is 1. Once LEN bytes have gone out or come in, a NACK (on master reads) and a STOP are generated.
15TENBITENR/W0Turns on 10-bit addressing. May be written together with ADDR to choose a 10-bit or 7-bit address transfer.
010-bit addressing off.
110-bit addressing on.
14HSR/W0Turns on High-speed mode for the present transfer, from repeated START to STOP. May be written together with ADDR for a high-speed transfer.
0High-speed transfer off.
1High-speed transfer on.
13LENENR/W0Turns on automatic transfer length.
0Automatic length off.
1Automatic length on.
10:0ADDRR/W0x0A write starts an operation that depends on the bus state. When unknown: INTFLAG.MB and STATUS.BUSERR go to 1 and the operation ends. When busy: the master waits for the bus to go idle. When idle: the master sends a START and the address; if it is acknowledged, SCL is kept low and both STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB go to 1. When owner: a repeated START is made, preceded by the acknowledge action if the last transaction was a read; this write is made while INTFLAG.MB or INTFLAG.SB is 1. The whole address is sent whether arbitration is won or lost; after a loss only ones are sent for the rest of it. The write clears the flags BUSERR and ARBLOST in STATUS and MB and SB in INTFLAG. Reading ADDR at any time leaves the bus alone. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.

DATADatap. 572

offset 0x18 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W · write-synchronized, read-synchronized

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7:0DATAR/W0x0Reads the receive buffer and writes the transmit buffer. Data is read or written correctly only while the master holds SCL low (STATUS.CLKHOLD = 1), except for reading the last byte after a STOP has been sent. An access to DATA.DATA starts I2C bus activity, set by CTRLB.ACKACT, CTRLB.SMEN and the access type (read or write). Outside smart mode, accesses need no synchronization.
